subject: Mechanical Engineering
title: Turbochargers: Exhaust-Powered Boost
description: Learn Turbochargers: Exhaust-Powered Boost in one minute.

hook.text: Exhaust gas is waste energy. A turbo recycles it for more power.

buildup.text: Hot exhaust spins a tiny turbine. That turbine drives a compressor.

discovery.text: The compressor forces more air into the engine, boosting power output.

twist.text: Turbo lag occurs because the turbine needs exhaust flow to spool up first.

climax.text: Modern turbos use twin-scroll or variable geometry to cut lag nearly to zero.

punchline.text: Waste gas in, free horsepower out. That's a turbo.

quiz.question: What causes turbo lag?
options: The compressor overheats and needs to cool down
The turbine needs exhaust flow to reach operating speed before it boosts
Oil takes time to reach the turbo bearings at startup
